abstract: |
  The custom AD Model Builder (ADMB) stock assessment model for eastern
  Bering Sea walleye pollock has a long history of operational use. This
  working paper evaluates an implementation of the 2024 assessment in the
  Stock Population and Recruitment Computational (SPoRC) framework. The
  corrected bridge normalizes bottom-trawl survey age compositions across ages
  1--15 and retains nominal multinomial sample sizes; ages 2--15 continue to
  define the survey abundance total. Spawning biomass, recruitment, population
  numbers at age, and selectivity agree with the corrected ADMB candidate at
  high numerical accuracy. The accepted ADMB assessment retains its management
  role. Updated afscOSA diagnostics, nine retrospective peels, a 30-dataset
  simulation self-test, and SPoRC-derived spmR projections all use the corrected
  fit. Fixing steepness preserves implementation equivalence. A correlated
  bivariate random walk on annual bottom-trawl survey midpoint and slope
  supports a sparse-metric SparseNUTS trial and identifies the remaining
  posterior geometry for further development.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(SPoRC)

  library(asar)

})

theme_set(ggthemes::theme_few())

repo_root <- if (file.exists("../config/base.yml")) ".." else "."
repo_path <- function(...) file.path(repo_root, ...)

report_gt <- function(data) {
  gt::gt(data) |>
    gt::tab_style(
      style = gt::cell_text(whitespace = "normal"),
      locations = gt::cells_column_labels()
    ) |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.width = gt::pct(100),
      table.layout = "fixed",
      table.font.size = gt::px(11),
      column_labels.padding = gt::px(6),
      data_row.padding = gt::px(5),
      container.overflow.x = "hidden"
    )
}
gt <- report_gt

cfg <- yaml::read_yaml(repo_path("config", "base.yml"))
asar_source_commit <- "e61c0f7d15569163fd5be8a7bfc582d5ca96c9af"

parse_asar_glossary <- function(path) {
  glossary_lines <- trimws(readLines(path, warn = FALSE))
  glossary_pattern <- "^\\\\newacronym\\{([^}]*)\\}\\{([^}]*)\\}\\{([^}]*)\\}$"
  glossary_matches <- regmatches(
    glossary_lines,
    regexec(glossary_pattern, glossary_lines)
  )
  glossary_matches <- glossary_matches[lengths(glossary_matches) == 4]
  data.frame(
    label = vapply(glossary_matches, `[[`, character(1), 2),
    Acronym = vapply(glossary_matches, `[[`, character(1), 3),
    Definition = vapply(glossary_matches, `[[`, character(1), 4),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

asar_package_glossary <- system.file(
  "glossary", "report_glossary.tex", package = "asar"
)
project_glossary_file <- repo_path("reporting", "report_glossary.tex")
project_glossary <- parse_asar_glossary(project_glossary_file)
asar_glossary <- parse_asar_glossary(asar_package_glossary)
glossary_key <- function(x) paste(x$label, x$Acronym, x$Definition, sep = "\r")
asar_shared_keys <- intersect(
  glossary_key(project_glossary), glossary_key(asar_glossary)
)
fit_path <- repo_path(cfg$composition_sample_sizes$model_family_fit)
input_path <- repo_path(cfg$composition_sample_sizes$model_family_inputs)
legacy_fit_path <- repo_path(cfg$composition_sample_sizes$legacy_bridge_fit)
legacy_input_path <- repo_path(cfg$composition_sample_sizes$legacy_bridge_inputs)
fit <- readRDS(fit_path)
fit_inputs <- readRDS(input_path)
legacy_fit <- readRDS(legacy_fit_path)
legacy_inputs <- readRDS(legacy_input_path)
dat <- readRDS(repo_path(cfg$composition_sample_sizes$corrected_data))
rep <- fit$report()
legacy_rep <- legacy_fit$report()
yrs <- dat$years
ages <- dat$ages
n_yrs <- length(yrs)

pct_diff <- function(x, ref) 100 * (x - ref) / pmax(abs(ref), .Machine$double.eps)
ssb_sporc <- as.vector(rep$SSB[1, 1, seq_len(n_yrs)])
rec_sporc <- as.vector(rep$Rec[1, 1, seq_len(n_yrs)])

bridge_ts <- rbind(
  data.frame(year = yrs, quantity = "Spawning biomass", model = "SPoRC", value = ssb_sporc),
  data.frame(year = yrs, quantity = "Spawning biomass", model = "Corrected ADMB candidate", value = as.vector(dat$admb$SSB)),
  data.frame(year = yrs, quantity = "Recruitment", model = "SPoRC", value = rec_sporc),
  data.frame(year = yrs, quantity = "Recruitment", model = "Corrected ADMB candidate", value = as.vector(dat$mle$Rec))
)

bridge_difference <- rbind(
  data.frame(year = yrs, quantity = "Spawning biomass", difference = pct_diff(ssb_sporc, dat$admb$SSB)),
  data.frame(year = yrs, quantity = "Recruitment", difference = pct_diff(rec_sporc, dat$mle$Rec))
)

bridge_metrics <- fit$case$bridge_metrics
fit_gradient <- max(abs(fit$sdrep$gradient.fixed))
bridge_parameters <- fit$env$parList(fit$env$last.par.best)
fixed_steepness_value <- 0.2 + 0.8 * plogis(bridge_parameters$steepness_h)

correction_effect <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("Spawning biomass", "Recruitment"),
  median_percent_change = c(
    median(abs(pct_diff(ssb_sporc, as.vector(legacy_rep$SSB[1, 1, seq_len(n_yrs)])))),
    median(abs(pct_diff(rec_sporc, as.vector(legacy_rep$Rec[1, 1, seq_len(n_yrs)]))))
  ),
  maximum_percent_change = c(
    max(abs(pct_diff(ssb_sporc, as.vector(legacy_rep$SSB[1, 1, seq_len(n_yrs)])))),
    max(abs(pct_diff(rec_sporc, as.vector(legacy_rep$Rec[1, 1, seq_len(n_yrs)]))))
  )
)
use_bts <- as.logical(fit_inputs$data$UseSrvAgeComps[1, , 1, 1])
bts_sample_size_audit <- data.frame(
  year = yrs[use_bts],
  corrected_nominal_iss = fit_inputs$data$ISS_SrvAgeComps[1, use_bts, 1, 1, 1],
  legacy_adjusted_iss = legacy_inputs$data$ISS_SrvAgeComps[1, use_bts, 1, 1, 1]
)
bts_sample_size_audit$legacy_multiplier <- with(
  bts_sample_size_audit, legacy_adjusted_iss / corrected_nominal_iss
)

surface_df <- function(sporc, admb, years, fleet) {
  s <- as.matrix(sporc)
  a <- as.matrix(admb)
  s <- s / max(s)
  a <- a / max(a)
  rbind(
    data.frame(year = rep(years, each = ncol(s)), age = rep(ages, times = nrow(s)), model = "SPoRC", value = as.vector(t(s)), fleet = fleet),
    data.frame(year = rep(years, each = ncol(a)), age = rep(ages, times = nrow(a)), model = "Corrected ADMB candidate", value = as.vector(t(a)), fleet = fleet)
  )
}

fish_sel <- surface_df(rep$fish_sel[1, 1, seq_len(n_yrs), 1, , 1, 1], dat$admb$sel_fsh, yrs, "Fishery")
bts_years <- 1982:2024
bts_idx <- match(bts_years, yrs)
bts_sel <- surface_df(rep$srv_sel[1, 1, bts_idx, 1, , 1, 1], dat$admb$sel_bts, bts_years, "BTS")
ats_years <- 1994:2024
ats_idx <- match(ats_years, yrs)
ats_sel <- surface_df(rep$srv_sel[1, 1, ats_idx, 1, , 1, 2], dat$admb$sel_ats, ats_years, "ATS")

fleet_table <- data.frame(
  component = c("Fishery CPUE", "Bottom trawl survey", "Acoustic trawl survey", "Vessel of opportunity", "Acoustic age 1"),
  likelihood = c("Normal", "Multivariate normal", "Lognormal", "Normal", "Lognormal"),
  selectivity = c("Fishery", "Logistic, time varying, free age 1", "Non-parametric random walk", "Shared with ATS", "Shared with ATS"),
  sporc_fleet = c("Fishery 1", "Survey 1", "Survey 2", "Survey 3", "Survey 4 (age 1 only)")
)

projection_dir <- repo_path("analysis", "outputs", "spmR_projection")
projection_alt2_dir <- repo_path(
  "analysis", "outputs", "spmR_projection_alt2_fixed1300"
)
projection_files <- c(
  manifest = file.path(projection_dir, "manifest.csv"),
  lineage = file.path(projection_dir, "base_lineage.csv"),
  input_audit = file.path(projection_dir, "projection_input_audit.csv"),
  metadata = file.path(projection_dir, "projection_run_metadata.csv"),
  tier3 = file.path(projection_dir, "tier3_seven_scenario_table.csv"),
  age_schedules = file.path(projection_dir, "projection_age_schedules.csv"),
  selected_simulations = file.path(projection_dir, "selected_simulations.csv"),
  detail = file.path(projection_dir, "spm_detail.csv"),
  alt2_detail = file.path(projection_alt2_dir, "spm_detail.csv")
)
missing_projection_files <- projection_files[!file.exists(projection_files)]
if (length(missing_projection_files) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Run analysis/run_sporc_spmr_projection.R before rendering. Missing: ",
    paste(basename(missing_projection_files), collapse = ", ")

}

projection_manifest <- utils::read.csv(projection_files[["manifest"]])
projection_lineage <- utils::read.csv(projection_files[["lineage"]])
projection_input_audit <- utils::read.csv(projection_files[["input_audit"]])
projection_metadata <- utils::read.csv(projection_files[["metadata"]])
if (as.character(utils::packageVersion("spmR")) != projection_metadata$spmR_version) {
  stop("The loaded spmR version differs from the projection lineage.")
}
expected_sporc_fit <- normalizePath(

)
if (normalizePath(projection_metadata$model_file, mustWork = TRUE) != expected_sporc_fit ||
    unname(tools::md5sum(expected_sporc_fit)) != projection_metadata$model_md5) {

}
if (projection_lineage$SPoRC_fit_case != "sporc_corrected_full_age_bts" ||
    any(grepl("rtmb_ebswp", unlist(projection_lineage), fixed = TRUE)) ||

projection_selected_simulations <- utils::read.csv(

)$Sim
projection_detail <- utils::read.csv(projection_files[["detail"]])
projection_alt2_detail <- utils::read.csv(projection_files[["alt2_detail"]])

projection_alt2_detail$B_B35 <- 100 *
  projection_alt2_detail$SSB / projection_alt2_detail$B35
projection_alt2_means <- aggregate(
  cbind(Catch, ABC, OFL, SSB, B_B35) ~ Year,

projection_alt1_detail <- subset(projection_detail, Alt == 1)
projection_alt1_detail$B_B35 <- 100 *
  projection_alt1_detail$SSB / projection_alt1_detail$B35
projection_alt1_means <- aggregate(
  cbind(SSB, Catch, ABC, OFL, F, B_B35) ~ Year,
  projection_alt1_detail,

projection_alt_desc <- data.frame(

  Name = c(

    "Author-specified ABC",
    "Average recent F",
    "Alternative SPR rate",
    "No fishing",

    "Applies recent average fishing mortality from the SPoRC assessment state.",
```

## Executive Summary

This page implements the [SPoRC single-region EBS pollock case study](https://chengmatt.github.io/SPoRC/dev/articles/f_single_region_ebs_pollock_case_study.html) as the SPoRC member of the EBS pollock model family. The primary lane uses a corrected ADMB model in which BTS observed age compositions sum to one across ages 1--15 and the multinomial retains the nominal sample sizes. Ages 2--15 continue to define the BTS abundance-total series.

The implementation reproduces the corrected 2024 ADMB candidate's spawning
biomass and recruitment series at near-numerical precision. The accepted ADMB
assessment retains its role as the management model.

The exact bridge has a maximum time-series difference of `r sprintf("%.3g", max(bridge_metrics$maximum_percent_difference))`%. The fitted solution has a positive-definite Hessian and a maximum fixed-effect gradient of `r sprintf("%.3g", fit_gradient)`. The evidence remains a development-model result, with ADMB retained as the management reference.

The corrected SPoRC fit reproduces six ADMB state and selectivity surfaces with
a maximum difference of
`r sprintf("%.3g", max(bridge_metrics$maximum_percent_difference))`%. Relative
to the legacy adjusted-ISS bridge, the correction changes spawning biomass by
at most `r sprintf("%.2f", correction_effect$maximum_percent_change[correction_effect$quantity == "Spawning biomass"])`%
and recruitment by at most
`r sprintf("%.2f", correction_effect$maximum_percent_change[correction_effect$quantity == "Recruitment"])`%.
All diagnostics and projections use the corrected lane.

Fixing steepness at `r sprintf("%.7f", fixed_steepness_value)`
preserves the corrected bridge at numerical precision. A correlated bivariate
random walk on annual BTS `log(a50)` and `log(k)` improves the maximum-
likelihood objective relative to independent increments. Section @sec-mcmc
reports the updated sparse-metric posterior diagnostics and retains the
maximum-likelihood bridge as the implementation basis.

The implementation uses SPoRC version `r as.character(packageVersion("SPoRC"))` from development branch `r cfg$sporc$ref` at commit `r substr(cfg$sporc$commit, 1, 8)`, and covers `r min(yrs)`–`r max(yrs)`.

### Position in the model family

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-family-flow
%%| fig-cap: "SPoRC's current position in the EBS pollock model-family workflow."
flowchart LR
  A["Accepted 2024 ADMB model"] --> C["Corrected full-age BTS ADMB candidate"]
  C --> B["SPoRC corrected implementation bridge"]
  D["Corrected ADMB and RTMB bridge artifacts"] --> B
  B --> G["Implementation-equivalence gate<br/>passed"]
  G --> R["Diagnostic and review gate<br/>development stage"]
  R -.-> U["Paired annual updates<br/>uncertainty and projections"]
  classDef accepted fill:#f5c242,stroke:#805f00,color:#172b3a,stroke-width:2px;
  classDef pass fill:#eef8f0,stroke:#2e7d32,color:#17451a,stroke-width:3px;
  classDef pending fill:#f4f0fa,stroke:#6d5cae,color:#17324d,stroke-width:2px;
  class A,D accepted;
  class B,G pass;
  class R,U pending;
```

The family registry is stored in `config/model_family.yml`. The exact bridge is the admission case. The comparisons exclude the earlier three-survey Beverton–Holt experiment because it uses a different model specification.

## Purpose and Scope

This working paper documents whether SPoRC can reproduce the principal
population dynamics and assessment outputs of the accepted 2024 eastern
Bering Sea pollock model. It serves as an implementation and methods
comparison rather than a full Stock Assessment and Fishery Evaluation chapter.

The paper therefore records:

- the model inputs and structural choices represented in SPoRC;
- agreement between the SPoRC and ADMB bridge calculations;
- fishery and survey selectivity comparisons;
- numerical and likelihood-accounting diagnostics; and
- the files and software revision needed to reproduce the analysis.

Fishery history, ecosystem narrative, projections, reference-point tables,
and harvest recommendations are outside the scope of this working paper.

## Initial SPoRC Developments

### Model Inputs

The model is single population, single region, single season, and single sex, with 15 ages, one fishery, and four SPoRC survey fleets. The fourth survey fleet represents the acoustic age-1 likelihood component, distinct from the observed survey fleets.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fleets
#| tbl-cap: "Index and survey components in the exact EBS pollock bridge."

gt(fleet_table) |>
  cols_label(component = "Component", likelihood = "Likelihood", selectivity = "Selectivity", sporc_fleet = "SPoRC representation")
```

### Selectivity specifications

Structural and selectivity choices adopted directly from the case study include:

- Ricker recruitment with a one-year lag, free initial numbers at age, the assessment recruitment penalties, and the steepness prior.
- Separate spawning, fishery, and survey weight-at-age arrays.
- The BTS full covariance likelihood and a free annual BTS age-1 selectivity value.
- Non-parametric random-walk fishery and ATS selectivity, with AVO sharing ATS selectivity.
- The acoustic age-1 abundance likelihood as survey fleet 4 with its own catchability.
- ADMB parameter values as the bridge starting point, with recruitment deviations solved by forward substitution and multiplicative catchabilities recovered analytically.

## ADMB Comparison Results

The bridge is evaluated at the accepted ADMB maximum-likelihood estimate before optimization. The objective there is `r sprintf("%.6f", fit$case$objective_at_admb_mle)` and the maximum absolute gradient is `r sprintf("%.3g", fit$case$maximum_gradient_at_admb_mle)`. Optimization leaves the solution effectively unchanged.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bridge
#| tbl-cap: "SPoRC and ADMB time-series differences."

gt(bridge_metrics) |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = c(median_percent_difference, maximum_percent_difference), decimals = 3) |>
  cols_label(quantity = "Quantity", median_percent_difference = "Median difference (%)", maximum_percent_difference = "Maximum difference (%)")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bridge
#| fig-cap: "SPoRC and ADMB spawning biomass and recruitment. Lines overlap at plotting precision."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

ggplot(bridge_ts, aes(year, value, color = model, linetype = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~quantity, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Value", color = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  ggthemes::theme_few()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bridge-difference
#| fig-cap: "Annual SPoRC-minus-ADMB differences. The vertical scale is percent."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(bridge_difference, aes(year, difference)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey65") +
  geom_line(color = "#005ea8", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~quantity, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Difference (%)") +
  ggthemes::theme_few()
```

The fitted object has `r length(fit$par)` free parameters, a final joint negative log likelihood of `r sprintf("%.3f", fit$rep$jnLL)`, a positive-definite Hessian, and a final maximum absolute fixed-effect gradient of `r sprintf("%.3g", fit_gradient)`. `nlminb` reports code `r fit$optim$convergence` ("`r fit$optim$message`"); the code remains disclosed even though the gradient, Hessian, and bridge trajectories reproduce the case-study solution.

### Corrected BTS age-composition treatment {#sec-corrected-bts-compositions}

The corrected ADMB candidate normalizes each observed BTS age composition over
ages 1--15, matching the prediction vector and the stated multinomial sample
space. It retains the nominal integer sample size for each year. Age-1
selectivity remains an annual free parameter, while a logistic midpoint and
slope define ages 2--15. The BTS abundance-total series continues to use the
ages 2--15 subtotal, preserving that observation model.

The legacy implementation normalized observed ages 1--15 by the ages 2--15
subtotal. Its adjusted SPoRC sample sizes reproduced that score algebraically.
The legacy multiplier has a median of
`r sprintf("%.3f", median(bts_sample_size_audit$legacy_multiplier))` and ranges
from `r sprintf("%.3f", min(bts_sample_size_audit$legacy_multiplier))` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(bts_sample_size_audit$legacy_multiplier))`. The corrected
form provides a coherent multinomial and a common sample-size basis across the
model-family tests.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-corrected-bts-effect
#| tbl-cap: "Change in SPoRC state outputs after correcting BTS composition normalization and retaining nominal sample sizes."

gt(correction_effect) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = where(is.numeric),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    quantity = "Quantity",
    median_percent_change = "Median change from legacy bridge (%)",
    maximum_percent_change = "Maximum change from legacy bridge (%)"
  )
```

The corrected ADMB-to-RTMB bridge differs in objective by 0.00038 and in key
outputs by at most 0.00049%. The corrected ADMB-to-SPoRC bridge in
@tbl-bridge provides the primary implementation regression gate. The legacy
artifact remains available for historical comparison.

```{r}
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.65) +
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-survey-selectivity

#| fig-width: 10

survey_sel <- rbind(bts_sel, ats_sel)
```

## Diagnostics

The corrected implementation-equivalence result is strong: spawning biomass,
recruitment, population numbers at age, and selectivity reproduce the corrected
ADMB candidate at high numerical accuracy. OSA, retrospective, self-test,
SparseNUTS, and projection products all trace to this corrected fit or its
stated fixed-steepness and parameter-RW derivatives.

ADMB and SPoRC retain engine-specific likelihood constants and reporting
layouts. State, fitted-surface, gradient, Hessian, and within-engine objective
checks therefore provide the regression gates used here.

```{r}
#| label: setup-diagnostics
#| include: false

diag_dir <- repo_path(cfg$paths$outputs_dir, "family_diagnostics")
retro <- readRDS(file.path(diag_dir, "retro_9.rds"))
retro_relative <- readRDS(file.path(diag_dir, "retro_9_relative.rds"))
peel_number <- as.integer(retro_relative$peel)
terminal_retro <- retro_relative[
  peel_number > 0 & retro_relative$Year == (length(yrs) - peel_number),
]
mohn <- aggregate(rd ~ Type, terminal_retro, mean)
names(mohn)[2] <- "mohn_rho"
retro_status <- unique(retro[c("peel", "pdHess", "max_grad", "convergence")])
self_test_summary <- read.csv(file.path(diag_dir, "self_test_30_summary.csv"))
osa <- readRDS(file.path(
  diag_dir, "osa", "sporc_corrected_full_age_bts_afscosa.rds"
))
retro_design <- read.csv(file.path(diag_dir, "retro_9_data_availability.csv"))

decode_mvrw_parameter <- function(label) {
  base <- sub("\\[.*$", "", label)
  has_index <- grepl("\\[[0-9]+\\]$", label)
  index <- if (has_index) {
    as.integer(sub(".*\\[([0-9]+)\\]$", "\\1", label))
  } else {
    1L
  }
  parameter_positions <- which(names(bts_mvrw_fit$par) == base)
  mle <- if (index <= length(parameter_positions)) {
    unname(bts_mvrw_fit$par[parameter_positions[index]])
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }

  quantity <- base
  scope <- "Global model parameter"
  translation <- if (is.finite(mle)) sprintf("MLE = %.3f", mle) else ""

  if (base == "ln_srvsel_devs") {
    map_array <- array(
      as.integer(bts_mvrw_input$mapping[[base]]),
      dim = dim(bts_mvrw_input$parameters[[base]])
    )
    coordinate <- which(map_array == index, arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
    fleet_names <- c("BTS", "ATS", "Vessel of opportunity", "Acoustic age 1")
    fleet <- fleet_names[coordinate[5]]
    slot <- coordinate[3]
    quantity <- if (coordinate[5] == 1 && slot == 1) {
      "BTS log(a50)"
    } else if (coordinate[5] == 1 && slot == 2) {
      "BTS log(k)"
    } else {
      paste(fleet, "log-selectivity parameter", slot)
    }
    age_scope <- if (coordinate[5] == 1 && slot <= 2) {
      "ages 2–15"
    } else {
      paste0("age ", ages[slot])
    }
    scope <- paste0(yrs[coordinate[2]], "; ", age_scope)
    translation <- if (coordinate[5] == 1 && slot == 1) {
      sprintf("a50 = %.3f years", exp(mle))
    } else if (coordinate[5] == 1 && slot == 2) {
      sprintf("k = %.3f per year", exp(mle))
    } else {
      sprintf("exp(parameter) = %.3f", exp(mle))
    }
  } else if (base == "ln_fishsel_devs") {
    map_array <- array(
      as.integer(bts_mvrw_input$mapping[[base]]),
      dim = dim(bts_mvrw_input$parameters[[base]])
    )
    coordinate <- which(map_array == index, arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
    quantity <- "Fishery log-selectivity coefficient"
    scope <- paste0(
      yrs[coordinate[2]], "; age ", ages[coordinate[3]],
      "; fishery fleet ", coordinate[5]
    )
    translation <- sprintf("exp(coefficient) = %.3f", exp(mle))
  } else if (base == "ln_RecDevs") {
    quantity <- "Annual log recruitment deviation"
    scope <- paste0(yrs[index], "; age-1 recruitment")
    translation <- sprintf("Multiplier = %.3f", exp(mle))
  } else if (base == "ln_global_R0") {
    quantity <- "Global log(R0)"
    scope <- "Global; age-1 recruitment scale"
    translation <- sprintf("R0 = %s model abundance units", format(
      round(exp(mle)), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE
    ))
  }

  data.frame(
    sampler_label = label,
    model_quantity = quantity,
    model_scope = scope,
    mle_translation = translation,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

mvrw_trace_parameter_key <- do.call(

    snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$selected_parameters$pairs,

)
```

### OSA Residuals

The age-composition diagnostics use the nominal-ISS model-family lane and the updated
[afscOSA workflow](https://noaa-afsc.github.io/afscOSA/#interpretation-and-use-of-diagnostics)
from [pull request 10](https://github.com/noaa-afsc/afscOSA/pull/10), installed
from commit `r substr(osa$afscOSA_commit, 1, 8)`. The analysis passes SPoRC's
internal randomized OSA residuals to afscOSA for the fishery and BTS. This
preserves the composition likelihood and conditional calculation embedded in
SPoRC. The ATS calculation uses the afscOSA multinomial routine on ages 2–15,
the age range used by the fitted likelihood. SPoRC's current internal
composition packer also retains ATS age 1. The external calculation therefore
aligns the ATS diagnostic with the fitted data window.

The ATS 2020 input sample size equals one. Integer allocation across its
fractional age proportions yields zero counts, so the analysis excludes that
zero-information row. The remaining ATS series contains 18 composition years.
All randomized calculations use seed `r osa$seed`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-osa-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary statistics for nominal-ISS age-composition diagnostics."

gt(osa_summary_display) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      sdnr, lower_tail_2.5_pct, upper_tail_97.5_pct,
      aggregate_ISS, aggregate_ESS, max_abs_osa, max_abs_pearson
    ),
    decimals = 2
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    fleet = "Data source",
    method = "OSA source",
    year_span = "Years",
    years = "Composition years",
    bins = "Age bins",
    sdnr = "SDNR",
    lower_tail_2.5_pct = "Lower 2.5%",
    upper_tail_97.5_pct = "Upper 97.5%",
    aggregate_ISS = "ISS",
    aggregate_ESS = "ESS",
    max_abs_osa = "Maximum |OSA|",
    max_abs_pearson = "Maximum |Pearson|"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-osa-age-diagnostics
#| fig-cap: "Age-composition fit and residual diagnostics from afscOSA for the fishery, bottom trawl survey (BTS), and acoustic-trawl survey (ATS). Columns distinguish data sources. Rows show observed aggregate proportions with model expectations and 95% data intervals, quantile–quantile plots of randomized OSA residuals with SDNR and tail-reference intervals, OSA residual bubbles, and Pearson residual bubbles. Blue and red bubbles represent positive and negative residuals, respectively, and bubble area increases with residual magnitude. Pearson magnitudes above 6 are displayed at 6 for legibility; numerical summaries retain the raw values."
#| fig-alt: "A twelve-panel diagnostic figure arranged in three columns for fishery, BTS, and ATS and four rows for aggregate fits, OSA quantile–quantile plots, OSA residual bubbles, and Pearson residual bubbles."

knitr::include_graphics(file.path(diag_dir, "osa", "osa_age_diagnostics.png"))
```

The 42 corrected BTS annual sample sizes sum to
`r format(sum(bts_sample_size_audit$corrected_nominal_iss), big.mark = ",")`. afscOSA's
proportion-to-integer-count conversion produces the displayed aggregate ISS of
`r format(osa_bts$aggregate_ISS, big.mark = ",")`, matching the convention used
for the other model-family diagnostics.

The aggregate panels provide the first diagnostic. Observed proportions follow
the principal age patterns expected by the model, while departures at specific
ages identify where selectivity and composition assumptions merit attention.
The interval bars describe the spread of data generated from each fitted
composition distribution at the aggregate sample size; they differ from
parameter-confidence intervals.

The fishery SDNR is `r sprintf("%.2f", osa_fishery$sdnr)` and the ATS SDNR is
`r sprintf("%.2f", osa_ats$sdnr)`. Both values fall below their displayed 95%
standard-normal reference intervals, indicating narrower residual distributions
than the reference. Their aggregate ESS values exceed their ISS values,
consistent with realized aggregate variability equivalent to larger samples
than the input weighting. The fishery upper-tail quantile
(`r sprintf("%.2f", osa_fishery$upper_tail_97.5_pct)`) also shows compression.
ATS tail quantiles remain within their displayed reference intervals.

The BTS SDNR is `r sprintf("%.2f", osa_bts$sdnr)` and lies within its displayed
reference interval. Its lower-tail quantile
(`r sprintf("%.2f", osa_bts$lower_tail_2.5_pct)`) extends beyond the reference
interval, whereas its upper tail is compressed at
`r sprintf("%.2f", osa_bts$upper_tail_97.5_pct)`. The OSA and Pearson bubbles
localize these asymmetries across ages and years. afscOSA displays two fishery
Pearson values above 6 at the plotting cap; the largest raw value is
`r sprintf("%.2f", osa_fishery$max_abs_pearson)`.

These diagnostics jointly describe model-data compatibility. The aggregate
fits, Q-Q behavior, tail statistics, and residual patterns guide investigation
of selectivity, sample weighting, and temporal structure. Their combined
evidence supports model refinement more effectively than a single threshold or
pass/fail decision.

### Retrospective patterns

Nine retrospective peels terminate in 2023–2015. Each active contemporary
data series retains the availability lag represented in the 2024 model. The
fishery age compositions have a one-year lag: the 2023 peel uses compositions
through 2022, and subsequent peels continue that one-year offset. Survey
indices and survey age compositions use observations at or before each peel's
terminal year according to their historical sampling schedules. The historical
fishery CPUE series retains its 1976 endpoint.

Each peel constrains fishery and survey selectivity in its terminal year to the
preceding year's selectivity. This constraint includes the BTS age-1
selectivity deviation. The authoritative 2024 full fit remains unchanged.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-retro-design
#| tbl-cap: "Data-availability and terminal-selectivity audit for nine SPoRC retrospective peels."

gt(retro_audit) |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = maximum_terminal_selectivity_difference, decimals = 2) |>
  cols_label(
    peel = "Peel",
    terminal_year = "Terminal year",
    fishery_compositions_through = "Fishery ages through",
    maximum_terminal_selectivity_difference = "Maximum terminal selectivity difference"
  )
```

All nine truncated fits have positive-definite Hessians. Their maximum
fixed-effect gradients range from
`r sprintf("%.2g", min(retro_status$max_grad[retro_status$peel > 0]))` to
`r sprintf("%.2g", max(retro_status$max_grad[retro_status$peel > 0]))`.
The status table retains optimizer code 1 for transparency; the
positive-definite Hessians and gradients below $10^{-8}$ provide the supporting
numerical diagnostics.
The selectivity audit gives a maximum terminal-year difference of
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(retro_audit$maximum_terminal_selectivity_difference))`
across every peel and fleet, confirming the equality constraint.


### MCMC integrations {#sec-mcmc}

The steepness sensitivity fixes biological-scale steepness at
`r sprintf("%.7f", fixed_bridge_summary$fixed_steepness)`, the estimate from the
exact bridge, and reoptimizes every remaining free parameter. This removes one
posterior dimension while preserving the fitted stock-recruit relationship.
The sensitivity has 1,206 free parameters, a positive-definite Hessian, and a
maximum gradient of
`r format(fixed_bridge_summary$maximum_gradient, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)`.
Its objective differs from the estimated-steepness bridge by
`r format(fixed_bridge_summary$objective_difference_from_free_steepness, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fixed-steepness-bridge
#| tbl-cap: "Bridge sensitivity after fixing steepness at the exact-bridge estimate."

fixed_bridge_metrics |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = where(is.numeric), decimals = 3) |>
  cols_label(
    quantity = "Quantity",
    median_percent_difference_from_admb = "Median difference from ADMB (%)",
    maximum_percent_difference_from_admb = "Maximum difference from ADMB (%)",
    median_percent_difference_from_free_steepness =
      "Median difference from estimated-steepness SPoRC (%)",
    maximum_percent_difference_from_free_steepness =
      "Maximum difference from estimated-steepness SPoRC (%)"
  )
```

Maximum differences from the estimated-steepness SPoRC bridge remain below
`r format(max(fixed_bridge_metrics$maximum_percent_difference_from_free_steepness), scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)`%,
and maximum differences from ADMB remain below
`r format(max(fixed_bridge_metrics$maximum_percent_difference_from_admb), scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)`%.
Fixing steepness therefore preserves implementation equivalence at numerical
precision.

#### BTS parameter-level random walks

Two sensitivity models replace the 1983--2024 BTS age-specific curve-change
penalty with direct random walks on annual `log(a50)` and `log(k)`. Both retain
the 1982 curve anchor and fix the increment SDs at 0.120 and 0.305. The first
uses independent increments. The second uses the new SPoRC correlated
bivariate random walk with correlation -0.829, estimated empirically from the
exact-bridge maximum-likelihood deviations. The fixed hyperparameters make
this a targeted parameterization experiment rather than an empirical-Bayes
uncertainty analysis.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bts-parameter-rw
#| tbl-cap: "Maximum-likelihood diagnostics for BTS parameter-level random-walk sensitivities."
#| tbl-pos: H

bts_parameter_rw_summary |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    model = ifelse(model == "independent", "Independent RW", "Correlated RW"),
    increment_rms_a50 = fitted_increment_rms_log_a50,
    increment_rms_k = fitted_increment_rms_log_k,
    increment_correlation = fitted_increment_correlation,
    maximum_gradient,
    positive_definite_hessian,
    maximum_ssb_difference = maximum_ssb_percent_difference_from_exact_bridge,
    maximum_recruitment_difference =
      maximum_recruitment_percent_difference_from_exact_bridge
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      increment_rms_a50, increment_rms_k, increment_correlation,
      maximum_ssb_difference, maximum_recruitment_difference
    ),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = maximum_gradient, decimals = 2) |>
  cols_label(
    model = "BTS process",
    increment_rms_a50 = "RMS Δlog(a50)",
    increment_rms_k = "RMS Δlog(k)",
    increment_correlation = "Increment correlation",
    maximum_gradient = "Maximum gradient",
    positive_definite_hessian = "Positive-definite Hessian",
    maximum_ssb_difference = "Maximum SSB difference (%)",
    maximum_recruitment_difference = "Maximum recruitment difference (%)"
  )
```

Both parameter-level sensitivities reach positive-definite Hessians with
maximum gradients below $2\times10^{-11}$. The correlated random walk follows
the fitted increment dependence closely and stays nearer the exact bridge:
its maximum SSB difference is
`r sprintf("%.2f", bts_parameter_rw_summary$maximum_ssb_percent_difference_from_exact_bridge[bts_parameter_rw_summary$model == "correlated"])`%,
compared with
`r sprintf("%.2f", bts_parameter_rw_summary$maximum_ssb_percent_difference_from_exact_bridge[bts_parameter_rw_summary$model == "independent"])`%
for independent increments. These differences quantify a deliberate change in
regularization; the exact bridge continues to carry the implementation-
equivalence result.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bts-parameter-rw
#| fig-cap: "Maximum-likelihood BTS logistic midpoint and slope under the exact curve-level bridge and the two parameter-level random-walk sensitivities."
#| fig-alt: "Two time-series panels show annual BTS a50 and slope k from 1982 through 2024. Black lines show the exact bridge, orange dashed lines show independent parameter increments, and blue dotted lines show correlated increments."
#| fig-pos: H

knitr::include_graphics(repo_path(
  cfg$paths$outputs_dir,
  "figures",
  "bts_parameter_rw_mle.png"
))
```

[SparseNUTS](https://noaa-afsc.github.io/SparseNUTS/) was applied as a
developmental posterior-sampling integration around both SPoRC bridge modes
and the correlated BTS parameter-RW sensitivity.
The runner rebuilds each RTMB objective from its archived data and parameter
map, verifies the free-parameter names against the corresponding fit, and
restores its maximum-likelihood estimates before sampling. SparseNUTS selected
a dense metric for the bridge objectives. The correlated-RW run explicitly
sets `metric = "sparse"`, declares `ln_srvsel_devs` as an RTMB random-effect
block, and sets `laplace = FALSE`. SparseNUTS therefore samples the same
1,206-dimensional joint posterior while constructing the sparse joint
precision matrix, $Q$. The classification contains 910 fixed and 296 random
parameters; it changes the computational representation while preserving the
joint posterior target. Each run used four chains, 150 warmup iterations per
chain, and 1,000 retained iterations per chain with seed 99803.

Both updated runs use a target acceptance probability of 0.95 and maximum tree
depth of 12. The convergence gate requires
zero divergent transitions, zero maximum-tree-depth transitions, acceptable
energy behavior in every chain, and a maximum R-hat at or below 1.01.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sparsenuts
#| tbl-cap: "SparseNUTS diagnostics for corrected fixed-steepness SPoRC models."
#| tbl-pos: H

snuts_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    divergent_transitions = round(perc_divergent / 100 * chains * postwarmup_per_chain)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    model, adapt_delta, maximum_rhat, minimum_bulk_ess,
    divergent_transitions
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      adapt_delta, maximum_rhat, minimum_bulk_ess
    ),
    decimals = 2
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    model = "Model",
    adapt_delta = "Target acceptance",
    maximum_rhat = "Maximum R-hat",
    minimum_bulk_ess = "Minimum bulk ESS",
    divergent_transitions = "Divergences"
  )
```

The corrected fixed-steepness run
`r if (snuts_fixed_inference_gate) "met" else "failed"` the convergence gate,
so its draws
`r if (snuts_fixed_inference_gate) "support preliminary posterior summaries" else "remain unsuitable for posterior inference"`.
The weakest behavior identifies the parameter blocks that govern the next
reparameterization experiment. The maximum-likelihood bridge result and its
management interpretation remain unchanged.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sparsenuts-trace
#| fig-cap: "Post-warmup SparseNUTS traces for the six parameters with the weakest convergence diagnostics in the tuned fixed-steepness run. Colors distinguish the four chains."
#| fig-alt: "Six trace panels compare four corrected fixed-steepness SparseNUTS chains across 1,000 post-warmup iterations for global unfished recruitment and annual recruitment deviations."
#| fig-pos: H

knitr::include_graphics(repo_path(snuts_fixed_tuned$figures$trace))
```

The brackets in the sampler labels index positions in the free parameter vector;
@tbl-trace-parameter-key maps those positions to their model years and
natural-scale multipliers.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-trace-parameter-key
#| tbl-cap: "Model interpretation of the sampler labels in the fixed-steepness trace figure."
#| tbl-pos: H

trace_parameter_key |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    sampler_label = "Sampler label",
    model_quantity = "Model quantity",
    model_scope = "Year and age application",
    mle_translation = "Maximum-likelihood translation"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sparsenuts-pairs
#| fig-cap: "Post-warmup pairs plot for the six parameters with the weakest convergence diagnostics in the tuned fixed-steepness SparseNUTS run. Diagonal panels show marginal posterior densities, lower panels show joint draws, and upper panels show correlations."
#| fig-alt: "A six-by-six pairs matrix for the weakest-mixing parameters. Diagonal panels show marginal densities, lower panels show joint posterior draws, and upper panels show correlations. The global recruitment scale has strong negative correlations with five annual recruitment deviations, which have strong positive mutual correlations."
#| fig-pos: H

knitr::include_graphics(repo_path(snuts_fixed_tuned$figures$pairs))
```

The pairs matrix shows the strongest sampled dependence between
`ln_global_R0` and recruitment deviations for 1990, 1996, 1997, 1999, and
2013. Their correlations with the global recruitment scale range from -0.941
to -0.971, and their mutual correlations range from 0.917 to 0.955. These
relationships support the dense preconditioner and highlight the broader
recruitment-scale mixing problem.

#### Correlated BTS random-walk posterior trial

The correlated parameter-level random walk was sampled from its
maximum-likelihood solution with the same target acceptance probability and
tree-depth limit as the tuned bridge run. Four parallel chains use the same
validated maximum-likelihood initialization. The
sparse metric uses the 296 survey-selectivity deviations as the RTMB random
block and samples all 1,206 joint parameters with Laplace integration disabled.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sparsenuts-bts-mvrw
#| tbl-cap: "SparseNUTS diagnostics for the fixed-steepness model with a correlated BTS parameter-level random walk."
#| tbl-pos: H

snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric = snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$sampler_settings$metric,
    random_block = paste(
      snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$sampler_settings$random_effects,
      collapse = ", "
    ),
    divergent_transitions = round(
      perc_divergent / 100 * chains * postwarmup_per_chain
    ),
    maximum_tree_depth_transitions = round(
      perc_max_treedepth / 100 * chains * postwarmup_per_chain
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    metric, random_block, chains, warmup_per_chain, postwarmup_per_chain, maximum_rhat,
    minimum_bulk_ess, divergent_transitions,
    maximum_tree_depth_transitions, chains_below_ebfmi
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = maximum_rhat,
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = minimum_bulk_ess,
    decimals = 1
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    metric = "TMB metric",
    random_block = "RTMB random block",
    chains = "Chains",
    warmup_per_chain = "Warmup per chain",
    postwarmup_per_chain = "Retained per chain",
    maximum_rhat = "Maximum R-hat",
    minimum_bulk_ess = "Minimum bulk ESS",
    divergent_transitions = "Divergences",
    maximum_tree_depth_transitions = "Maximum tree depth",
    chains_below_ebfmi = "Low E-BFMI chains"
  )
```

The correlated-RW run
`r if (snuts_bts_mvrw_inference_gate) "met" else "failed"` the convergence
gate. It produced
`r round(snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$perc_divergent / 100 * snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$chains * snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$postwarmup_per_chain)`
divergent transitions, a maximum R-hat of
`r sprintf("%.3f", snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$maximum_rhat)`, and a minimum
bulk ESS of `r sprintf("%.1f", snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$minimum_bulk_ess)`.
It reached maximum tree depth in
`r format(round(snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$perc_max_treedepth / 100 * snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$chains * snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$postwarmup_per_chain), big.mark = ",")`
of the 4,000 retained transitions
(`r sprintf("%.2f", snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$perc_max_treedepth)`%) and
placed `r snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$rhat_above_1_05` parameters above an
R-hat of 1.05.
Relative to the tuned fixed-steepness bridge, divergences changed from
`r round(snuts_fixed_tuned_result$perc_divergent / 100 * snuts_fixed_tuned_result$chains * snuts_fixed_tuned_result$postwarmup_per_chain)`
to
`r round(snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$perc_divergent / 100 * snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$chains * snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$postwarmup_per_chain)`,
maximum R-hat changed from
`r sprintf("%.3f", snuts_fixed_tuned_result$maximum_rhat)` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$maximum_rhat)`, and minimum bulk
ESS changed from `r sprintf("%.1f", snuts_fixed_tuned_result$minimum_bulk_ess)`
to `r sprintf("%.1f", snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$minimum_bulk_ess)`. Any
divergent transition, maximum-tree-depth transition, or maximum R-hat above
1.01 keeps the draws exploratory under the stated gate.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sparsenuts-bts-mvrw-Q
#| fig-cap: "SparseNUTS joint precision and correlation structure for the correlated BTS parameter-level random-walk run. The upper triangle shows the structural nonzero pattern of Q; the lower triangle shows correlations implied by its inverse, with red positive and blue negative."
#| fig-alt: "A 1,206 by 1,206 matrix plot. The upper triangle shows blocks of structural connections and gaps in the joint precision matrix. The lower triangle shows broad positive correlation blocks in red and smaller negative blocks in blue."
#| fig-pos: H

knitr::include_graphics(repo_path(snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$figures$Q))
```

The joint precision matrix has dimension
`r paste0(snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$q_matrix_summary$dimension, " by ", snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$q_matrix_summary$dimension)`
and `r sprintf("%.2f", snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$q_matrix_summary$percent_zero)`%
structural zeros. The modest sparsity reflects broad coupling between annual
state and observation parameters, while the block pattern preserves enough
structure for SparseNUTS to construct its requested sparse preconditioner.
Constructing $Q$ took
`r sprintf("%.1f", snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$snuts_fit$timing$time.Q)` seconds, and
the four chains averaged
`r sprintf("%.2f", mean(snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$snuts_fit$timing$time.total) / 60)`
minutes each.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sparsenuts-bts-mvrw-trace
#| fig-cap: "Post-warmup traces for the six weakest-mixing parameters in the correlated BTS parameter-level random-walk run. Colors distinguish the four chains."
#| fig-alt: "Six trace panels compare four SparseNUTS chains for the parameters with the weakest convergence diagnostics under the correlated BTS random walk."
#| fig-pos: H

knitr::include_graphics(repo_path(snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$figures$trace))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sparsenuts-bts-mvrw-parameter-key
#| tbl-cap: "Model interpretation of the six weakest-mixing sampler labels under the correlated BTS random walk."
#| tbl-pos: H

mvrw_trace_parameter_key |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    sampler_label = "Sampler label",
    model_quantity = "Model quantity",
    model_scope = "Year and age application",
    mle_translation = "Maximum-likelihood translation"
  )
```

All six weakest-mixing parameters are annual survey-selectivity parameters.
@tbl-sparsenuts-bts-mvrw-parameter-key resolves each sampler index to its year,
age application, and natural-scale maximum-likelihood value.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sparsenuts-bts-mvrw-pairs
#| fig-cap: "Pairs plot for the six weakest-mixing parameters in the correlated BTS parameter-level random-walk run. Diagonal panels show marginal posterior densities, lower panels show joint draws, and upper panels show correlations."
#| fig-alt: "A six-by-six pairs matrix displays marginal posterior densities and pairwise dependence for the weakest-mixing correlated-RW parameters."
#| fig-pos: H

knitr::include_graphics(repo_path(snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse$figures$pairs))
```

The pairs matrix locates the remaining geometry in annual BTS selectivity.
Pairwise correlations among the six weakest-mixing deviations range from
-0.536 to 0.879. Together with the maximum R-hat of
`r sprintf("%.3f", snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$maximum_rhat)` and
`r sprintf("%.2f", snuts_bts_mvrw_sparse_result$perc_max_treedepth)`%
maximum-tree-depth rate, this concentration identifies the BTS selectivity
state vector and its sparse parameterization as the clearest next sampling
experiment.

## Projections {#sec-projections}

This projection section reads the saved `sporc_corrected_full_age_bts` fit and
its matching corrected input artifact directly. The corrected SPoRC bridge
supplies a complete Standard Projection Model input directory for
`spmR`. The adapter extracts
terminal numbers at age and biological schedules, carries forward terminal
fishery selectivity, calculates recent fishing mortality from the same
age-6 convention used in the reference projection, and writes `pm.prj` and
`spm.dat`. The runner compiles the ADMB projection engine from the `spm.tpl`
source installed with the recorded `spmR` version. A field-level audit compares
each written vector with the saved SPoRC state and enforces a maximum relative
formatting difference of $5\times10^{-7}$.

The SPoRC and RTMB projections agree closely because both implementation
bridges reproduce the corrected ADMB candidate's population state at high
numerical accuracy. The projections reported here read the SPoRC fit and input
artifacts listed in @tbl-sporc-spmr-projection-files; their source paths and hashes
remain distinct from the RTMB projection artifacts.

The seven-alternative run uses the 2024 terminal-year maximum-likelihood
bridge, fixes 2025 and 2026 catches at 1,350 thousand t, and projects 1,000
simulations through 2038. This is a development-model projection sensitivity;
the accepted assessment remains the source for management advice.

## ESP-linked Recruitment Research

Environmental and ecosystem-linked recruitment models lie beyond the exact
implementation bridge tested here. The current SPoRC configuration retains
the accepted Ricker stock-recruit relationship and holds the recruitment
hypothesis constant during implementation testing. A future research stage
could compare environmental covariates or dynamic recruitment structures
against this validated bridge, with each alternative evaluated using common
data, convergence criteria, retrospective behavior, and simulation recovery.

## Summary

The SPoRC bridge achieves its primary implementation goal: it reproduces the
corrected full-age BTS ADMB candidate's spawning biomass, recruitment,
population state, and selectivity outputs at high numerical accuracy. The
correction yields unit-sum observed and predicted BTS compositions across ages
1--15 with nominal sample sizes, while ages 2--15 continue to define the BTS
abundance total. The result supports continued development of SPoRC as a
member of the EBS pollock model family, while the accepted ADMB assessment
remains the management reference. Fixing steepness preserves the corrected
bridge. The correlated BTS parameter-level random walk improves the
maximum-likelihood objective and provides the sparse-metric posterior trial.
The stated convergence gate determines the appropriate use of those draws.

The current results support review of the corrected implementation bridge,
positive retrospective bias, `r unique(self_test_summary$failed)` self-test
failures, and updated SparseNUTS convergence findings. They support continued
SPoRC development while retaining the accepted management model.

The immediate work sequence retains the corrected ADMB and RTMB comparisons as
regression gates after SPoRC package, likelihood, or data changes. Subsequent
diagnostics should use the corrected bridge configuration. Reparameterizing
the weakest-mixing block and repeating the correlated-RW SparseNUTS gate will
establish readiness for using MCMC draws in uncertainty summaries or
projections.

## Appendix {.unnumbered}

### Acronyms {.unnumbered}

This appendix follows the [Alaska Stock Assessment Report (ASAR) package](https://github.com/nmfs-ost/asar)
glossary convention. The project glossary uses ASAR's `\newacronym` format,
retains shared package entries where available, and adds terms specific to the
SPoRC bridge and its diagnostics.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-acronyms
#| tbl-cap: "Acronyms used in this working paper."

project_glossary |>
  dplyr::select(Acronym, Definition) |>
  gt::gt()
```
